title: What Happens If You Swallow a Watermelon Seed?
sources: Mayo Clinic, 'Watermelon seeds: Are they safe to eat?' (seeds pass through digestive system undigested; no plants grow in stomach)
WebMD, 'Watermelon seeds nutrition' (seeds contain protein, magnesium, iron; sprouted seeds are nutritious)
Cleveland Clinic, 'Can you digest seeds?' (seeds are indigestible; they pass through whole)

lines.text: What happens if you swallow a watermelon seed?
Your mom probably told you a watermelon would grow in your stomach.

lines.text: The seed goes down, and your stomach acid starts working on it.
But the seed's tough outer shell protects it from being digested.
lines.caps: Tough *outer shell | protects it | from being *digested

lines.text: So it passes through your entire digestive system, completely unchanged.
lines.caps: Passes through | your entire *digestive system | completely *unchanged

lines.text: A day or two later, it comes out the other end, still a seed.

lines.text: But here is the twist: if you sprout the seeds first, they become a superfood.

lines.text: Sprouted watermelon seeds are packed with protein, magnesium, and iron.
